name: FDA and Health Canada
description: FDA and Health Canada control approvals, inspections, labels, safety action and manufacturing compliance in the US and Canada. The immediate issue is accelerated-approval evidence, post-market commitments, data integrity and inspection readiness. Its decisions or actions can delay or withdraw products, require warnings, recalls or remediation.
urgency_rationale: Regulatory action can immediately affect two large markets and global confidence.
intel_dossier: 🔎 FDA drug development and approval: FDA sets the US approval and lifecycle requirements for drugs. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-approval-process-drugs

🔎 Health Canada drug shortages: Health Canada coordinates prevention and mitigation of nationally significant shortages. | https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/drug-shortages.html
🔎 FDA safety and availability: FDA publishes safety communications, recalls and post-market information. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability
alternate_rationale: Keep Satisfied may fit a stable mature portfolio, but active submissions and post-market obligations require close management.

engagement_tactics.label: Create a single evidence room and joint workplan with FDA and Health Canada
engagement_tactics.rationale: Gives the authority traceable data, named owners and early visibility of corrective action.

engagement_tactics.label: Rely mainly on trade-association lobbying
engagement_tactics.rationale: Collective advocacy cannot substitute for company-specific compliance evidence.

engagement_tactics.label: Wait for a notice, inspection or deficiency letter
engagement_tactics.rationale: Reactive engagement reduces room to correct problems before enforcement.

name: CMS, Provincial Drug Plans and PMPRB
description: CMS, Provincial Drug Plans and PMPRB shape negotiated prices, formulary access and affordability expectations. The immediate issue is Medicare negotiation, Canadian price review, evidence and patient affordability. Its decisions or actions can compress net price, restrict access or reset benchmarks.
urgency_rationale: Negotiation and listing cycles create direct revenue and access deadlines.
intel_dossier: 🔎 CMS drug price negotiation: CMS implements Medicare drug-price negotiation and related manufacturer requirements. | https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/medicare-prescription-drug-affordability/overview/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program
🔎 PMPRB: PMPRB protects Canadians from excessive patented-medicine prices and reports on market trends. | https://pmprb-cepmb.gc.ca/

🔎 Health Canada drug shortages: Health Canada coordinates prevention and mitigation of nationally significant shortages. | https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/drug-shortages.html
alternate_rationale: Keep Satisfied is possible outside selected products, but high-spend drugs need close engagement.

engagement_tactics.label: Co-develop an evidence, access and supply plan with CMS, Provincial Drug Plans and PMPRB
engagement_tactics.rationale: Links price or procurement discussions to outcomes, affordability and continuity of supply.

engagement_tactics.label: Offer a blanket discount with no access conditions
engagement_tactics.rationale: Sacrifices value without ensuring uptake, adherence or patient access.

engagement_tactics.label: Escalate the negotiation through public criticism
engagement_tactics.rationale: Hardens positions and can damage trust with other payers.

name: PBMs, Insurers and Integrated Delivery Networks
description: PBMs, Insurers and Integrated Delivery Networks control formulary position, utilisation management, rebates and patient pathways. The immediate issue is net cost, outcomes evidence, prior authorisation, biosimilar strategy and supply. Its decisions or actions can exclude products or impose access friction at scale.
urgency_rationale: A single formulary decision can move large patient volumes.
intel_dossier: 🔎 CMS drug price negotiation: CMS implements Medicare drug-price negotiation and related manufacturer requirements. | https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/medicare-prescription-drug-affordability/overview/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program
🔎 FTC pharmaceuticals: FTC enforces competition law in pharmaceutical markets. | https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/topics/competition-enforcement/pharmaceuticals
🔎 HHS OIG compliance guidance: HHS OIG publishes compliance guidance relevant to healthcare arrangements and federal programmes. | https://oig.hhs.gov/compliance/compliance-guidance/
alternate_rationale: Keep Satisfied may work for differentiated products with stable contracts; renewals and competitive launches require close management.

engagement_tactics.label: Co-develop an evidence, access and supply plan with PBMs, Insurers and Integrated Delivery Networks
engagement_tactics.rationale: Links price or procurement discussions to outcomes, affordability and continuity of supply.

engagement_tactics.label: Offer a blanket discount with no access conditions
engagement_tactics.rationale: Sacrifices value without ensuring uptake, adherence or patient access.

engagement_tactics.label: Escalate the negotiation through public criticism
engagement_tactics.rationale: Hardens positions and can damage trust with other payers.

name: Patient Advocates, Caregivers and Trial Participants
description: Patient Advocates, Caregivers and Trial Participants experience treatment benefit, safety, affordability and access barriers directly. The immediate issue is copay burden, transparent evidence, diversity, consent and shortage communication. Its decisions or actions can influence regulators, legislators, payers and litigation.
urgency_rationale: Health and affordability concerns can escalate rapidly and credibly.
intel_dossier: 🔎 FDA safety and availability: FDA publishes safety communications, recalls and post-market information. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability

🔎 CMS drug price negotiation: CMS implements Medicare drug-price negotiation and related manufacturer requirements. | https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/medicare-prescription-drug-affordability/overview/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program

🔎 Health Canada drug shortages: Health Canada coordinates prevention and mitigation of nationally significant shortages. | https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/drug-shortages.html
alternate_rationale: Manage Closely applies for rare diseases, safety controversies or severe access constraints.

engagement_tactics.label: Create a representative forum with independent data review for Patient Advocates, Caregivers and Trial Participants
engagement_tactics.rationale: Combines voice, verifiable evidence and a public commitments tracker.

engagement_tactics.label: Replace consultation with local donations
engagement_tactics.rationale: Philanthropy does not address rights, exposure or operational impacts.

engagement_tactics.label: Engage only through local political intermediaries
engagement_tactics.rationale: Excludes affected groups and makes consent appear managed rather than earned.

name: Physicians, Health Systems and Pharmacists
description: Physicians, Health Systems and Pharmacists determine prescribing, pathways, infusion capacity and real-world monitoring. The immediate issue is clinical differentiation, administrative burden, reimbursement and supply. Its decisions or actions can accelerate, restrict or abandon adoption.
urgency_rationale: Provider workflows and staffing can be the binding constraint after approval.
intel_dossier: 🔎 FDA drug development and approval: FDA sets the US approval and lifecycle requirements for drugs. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-approval-process-drugs

🔎 CMS drug price negotiation: CMS implements Medicare drug-price negotiation and related manufacturer requirements. | https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/medicare-prescription-drug-affordability/overview/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program
🔎 FDA safety and availability: FDA publishes safety communications, recalls and post-market information. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability
alternate_rationale: Keep Informed is adequate for stable products; complex launches require joint implementation.

engagement_tactics.label: Build a joint service, quality and continuity plan with Physicians, Health Systems and Pharmacists
engagement_tactics.rationale: Makes performance expectations explicit and creates early-warning triggers.

engagement_tactics.label: Promise priority supply to every major account
engagement_tactics.rationale: Conflicting commitments become impossible to honour during a disruption.

engagement_tactics.label: Limit contact to sales teams
engagement_tactics.rationale: Commercial dialogue alone misses quality, safety and operational dependencies.

name: CMOs, Wholesalers and Specialty Distributors
description: CMOs, Wholesalers and Specialty Distributors control critical manufacturing capacity, channel inventory and cold-chain execution. The immediate issue is quality events, allocation, serialization, shortage notices and recall readiness. Its decisions or actions can create national shortages, diversion or delayed treatment.
urgency_rationale: Supply failures trigger immediate patient and regulator consequences.
intel_dossier: 🔎 FDA drug shortages: FDA works with manufacturers to prevent and mitigate shortages. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability/drug-shortages

🔎 Health Canada drug shortages: Health Canada coordinates prevention and mitigation of nationally significant shortages. | https://www.canada.ca/en/health-canada/services/drugs-health-products/drug-products/drug-shortages.html
🔎 FDA safety and availability: FDA publishes safety communications, recalls and post-market information. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability
alternate_rationale: Keep Informed fits diversified, low-risk channels; specialty and sole-source products need close control.

engagement_tactics.label: Agree inventory, traceability and recall protocols with CMOs, Wholesalers and Specialty Distributors
engagement_tactics.rationale: Clarifies decision rights and reduces delay when safety or shortage events occur.

engagement_tactics.label: Push excess inventory into the channel
engagement_tactics.rationale: Creates expiry, grey-market and trust risks.

engagement_tactics.label: Share forecasts only after production is fixed
engagement_tactics.rationale: Late information prevents coordinated capacity and allocation decisions.

name: Scientists, Manufacturing Staff and Sales Teams
description: Scientists, Manufacturing Staff and Sales Teams generate evidence, manufacture products and execute commercial conduct. The immediate issue is speak-up culture, incentive design, skills, safety and restructuring. Its decisions or actions can prevent or expose quality, research-integrity and promotion failures.
urgency_rationale: Turnover or weak incentives can quickly undermine regulated processes.
intel_dossier: 🔎 HHS OIG compliance guidance: HHS OIG publishes compliance guidance relevant to healthcare arrangements and federal programmes. | https://oig.hhs.gov/compliance/compliance-guidance/
🔎 FDA drug development and approval: FDA sets the US approval and lifecycle requirements for drugs. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-approval-process-drugs
🔎 FDA safety and availability: FDA publishes safety communications, recalls and post-market information. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/drug-safety-and-availability
alternate_rationale: Manage Closely applies during integration, site remediation or major workforce change.

engagement_tactics.label: Negotiate a safety, skills and workload plan with Scientists, Manufacturing Staff and Sales Teams
engagement_tactics.rationale: Uses formal worker voice and measurable actions to reduce operational and labour risk.

engagement_tactics.label: Use attendance bonuses to suppress grievances
engagement_tactics.rationale: Treats symptoms, discourages reporting and can worsen fatigue-related risk.

engagement_tactics.label: Communicate only through line supervisors
engagement_tactics.rationale: Workers need trusted escalation channels and protection from retaliation.

name: Shareholders, Creditors and Activist Investors
description: Shareholders, Creditors and Activist Investors allocate capital and challenge pipeline, pricing and portfolio choices. The immediate issue is launch performance, regulatory risk, patent cliffs and capital allocation. Its decisions or actions can reprice equity, constrain debt or seek board change.
urgency_rationale: A clinical, pricing or regulatory event can change valuation instantly.
intel_dossier: 🔎 FDA drug development and approval: FDA sets the US approval and lifecycle requirements for drugs. | https://www.fda.gov/drugs/development-approval-process-drugs

🔎 CMS drug price negotiation: CMS implements Medicare drug-price negotiation and related manufacturer requirements. | https://www.cms.gov/initiatives/medicare-prescription-drug-affordability/overview/medicare-drug-price-negotiation-program
🔎 FTC pharmaceuticals: FTC enforces competition law in pharmaceutical markets. | https://www.ftc.gov/news-events/topics/competition-enforcement/pharmaceuticals
alternate_rationale: Manage Closely applies during proxy pressure, major readouts, transactions or guidance resets.

engagement_tactics.label: Brief Shareholders, Creditors and Activist Investors on material risks, capital needs, milestones and downside cases
engagement_tactics.rationale: Allows investors to test execution quality rather than rely on broad commitments.

engagement_tactics.label: Describe the exposure as immaterial until a charge is booked
engagement_tactics.rationale: Delayed disclosure increases surprise and credibility risk.

engagement_tactics.label: Promise a fixed outcome that management cannot control
engagement_tactics.rationale: Overconfidence creates litigation and trust risk if regulation or markets change.
